externalReferences.title: Postman: write response tests
externalReferences.summary: Use named post-response assertions on status, headers and returned data. Request-level checks can cover one operation; collection/folder scripts can share checks. The supplied collection includes original examples using pm.test and pm.expect.

externalReferences.title: Postman: variables and environments
externalReferences.summary: Parameterize the base URL and demo credentials, rather than changing every request. Choose a variable scope deliberately and keep real secrets out of shared exports. The supplied collection uses local teaching tokens only.

externalReferences.title: Postman: run a collection
externalReferences.summary: Run requests in a reproducible order and inspect their assertion results. A response can save an ID or validator for the next request. Use an isolated fixture and deliberate setup/cleanup rather than relying on yesterday’s server state.

externalReferences.title: Swagger: OpenAPI and documentation tools
externalReferences.summary: OpenAPI is the description format; Swagger supplies tools such as editors, documentation renderers and generators. A generated UI or SDK does not establish authorization or business correctness. This linked guide uses OpenAPI 3.0; this course’s contract examples use 3.1.

externalReferences.title: RFC 9457: Problem Details
externalReferences.summary: Problem Details gives HTTP APIs a reusable error representation. Type identifies the kind of problem; title/detail help people; status agrees with the origin’s HTTP response. Extensions can carry safe validation details. Never expose implementation secrets in error payloads.

externalReferences.title: RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 security guidance
externalReferences.summary: Read this current security guidance alongside the OAuth framework. Authorization code with PKCE is an important modern pattern; avoid treating legacy implicit/password examples as a default. Follow the identity provider’s validated flow and token-handling guidance.

externalReferences.title: GraphQL: learning guide
externalReferences.summary: GraphQL specifies a typed schema and query execution model. Learn how a client selects fields and how servers resolve them; HTTP transport alone does not define those operations. Continue in the separate graphql-lms for depth.

externalReferences.title: gRPC: introduction
externalReferences.summary: gRPC defines services and remote calls, commonly using Protocol Buffers and generated stubs. It supports unary and streaming call patterns. Choose it according to client/runtime needs, not merely because a payload is smaller.
